transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm explaining this right, but... I guess what brings me in is that I just can't seem to keep my mind on one thing anymore. It's probably just a minor thing, but at work—I do inventory and freight at a warehouse—every little noise is suddenly distracting me. 

If a beeper goes off, or I hear a forklift alarm, or even just someone moving a pallet nearby, it completely pulls me off my count. And then... well, it's a bit embarrassing to admit, but I'll realize I've accidentally put the wrong numbers into the inventory system. I really pride myself on doing good work and being reliable, so messing up the count has been bothering me. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job, and I was hoping maybe you could help me focus a bit better.
Has this kind of distraction or trouble focusing been happening in other parts of your life, like at home or while driving, or does it seem to only happen at work?

Oh, um... I don't really think so? At least, I haven't really noticed it much outside of the warehouse. I mean, maybe I'll get a little sidetracked at home if the TV is too loud, but nothing major. I try really hard to keep things nice and organized at the house, so I don't think it's a problem there. 

And I'm always very careful when I'm driving, so I haven't had any issues with that, thank goodness. I hope that's a good sign? I really just noticed it at work mostly because I want to make sure I'm doing a perfect job for my supervisor. Am I giving you the right kind of information? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.

Have you ever found yourself struggling to stay focused or being easily distracted in situations that require sustained attention, like reading, following conversations, or completing tasks, even if those situations aren’t at work?

No, not really. I mean, I love reading, and I can usually sit down with a good book and just... read for a while. I don't really lose my place or anything. And conversations are fine! I'm a very good listener, I promise. I always make sure to pay attention when people are talking to me. 

If I'm doing chores around the house, like folding laundry or doing the dishes, I just get them done. I like to keep a tidy house, so I make sure I finish what I start. I don't think I have any problems with that sort of thing... I hope that's okay? I just really think it's the warehouse noises that are throwing me off. Does that sound like a normal thing to happen?
Do you ever feel restless or find yourself needing to be constantly moving, like you can't sit still for very long?

Well... I wouldn't say I'm restless in a bad way. I mean, I know some people get all fidgety and can't sit through a movie, but it's not like that. It's more like... I just have a lot of productive energy lately? 

Like, usually after a long shift at the warehouse, I'd be pretty worn out. But recently, I come home and I'm just sort of... buzzing, I guess? Instead of sitting on the couch—which just feels a little impossible right now, honestly—I'll start reorganizing the kitchen cabinets or going out to the garage to sort through the storage bins. I just like to keep busy and make sure the house is in top shape. That's a good thing, right? Being productive instead of just being lazy after work? I hope it doesn't sound like I'm overly anxious or anything, I just really enjoy getting things done.

Can you tell me a bit more about this feeling of buzzing or being unable to sit still? Does it ever happen even when you’re not planning to do something productive, like when you’re trying to relax or fall asleep?

Oh, um... no, definitely not when I'm trying to sleep. I know how important a good night's rest is, especially with my job moving freight and everything, so I'm very good about going to bed at a reasonable hour. I don't really lie there tossing and turning or feeling jittery, thank goodness. 

And if I do decide I just want to sit and relax for a bit, I can. It's really just that I prefer to be up and doing things if there are chores to be done, you know? I don't like leaving a mess. I hope that makes sense... I just want to make sure I'm not making it sound like I'm out of control or anything, because I really do rest just fine when it's time to. Does that answer your question okay?
Have you noticed yourself doing things very quickly or with more intensity than usual, like rushing through tasks or taking on more projects than you normally would?

Well, um... I guess I have been taking on a little more than usual, but it's all good things, I promise! I just want to be helpful, you know? 

Like at work—moving freight can be dangerous if you aren't careful, so I've been volunteering for some extra safety-improvement projects. Just trying to make sure everyone stays safe. And, well, outside of work, I've been signing up for a few more art workshops than I normally would. I've been making all these lists and schedules to keep it all organized... honestly, it feels a bit like I'm running a whole operation! But I'm managing it all just fine, really. I just like to be involved and make the most of my time. That's a positive thing, isn't it? Being proactive like that?
Have you noticed that your mood has been unusually high, elated, or irritable lately, where you feel like you don't need as much rest or sleep because you're so energized?

Well, um... like I said, I really do make sure I get my sleep. But as for my mood... I guess it has been really, really good? Maybe... well, maybe almost a little too upbeat on some days, if that makes sense? I just get this wonderful feeling like I can tackle anything—like I could fix up the whole house and sort out the entire warehouse all before dinner. It's a nice feeling to have that much drive. 

But, um... I do feel a little guilty because... well, if my husband questions one of my plans while I'm trying to do all this, I've noticed I kind of... snap at him? Just over really small things. I don't mean to be irritable at all, I just get so focused on getting everything done for us. It's normal to get a little frustrated when someone interrupts your flow when you're working hard, right? I hope that doesn't make me sound awful, I really do try to be a patient wife.
Have there been specific periods of time when you felt unusually energetic, upbeat, or irritable for most of the day, nearly every day, even if only lasting a few days?

Oh, um... well, no, I don't think so. I mean, I have those days where I'm just feeling really good and getting a lot done, like I mentioned with the art classes and the safety projects. But it's not like it's taking over my whole life for days on end or anything. 

I really just have normal good days, you know? Like anyone else. I don't think I've had any stretches where I'm just constantly, unusually... well, whatever you called it, for most of the day, every day. I try to keep things pretty balanced and normal. I hope that's the right answer... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need, but I really don't think I've had anything quite like what you're describing. That's okay, right?

Have there ever been a few days in a row where you felt so energized, your mood was unusually high or irritable, and you were doing things much more quickly or intensely than usual — even if it was something positive like starting new projects, cleaning, or working faster — and this behavior was noticeable enough that others might have commented on it?

Um, no, I... I don't believe so. I mean, I know I just talked about having those really good days where I'm getting a lot done around the house or at the warehouse, but... it's never been like a whole string of days where I'm acting out of the ordinary. 

I really do try to keep myself in check so I don't bother anyone. My husband might say I'm being a busybody sometimes, but he just means it affectionately, you know? He's never sat me down and told me I was acting strange or too intense for days on end. I just like to be helpful and keep things moving. I really hope I'm not giving you the wrong impression... I just don't think I've ever had a period like that where people were worried about me or anything. Is that what you were looking for? I just want to be honest with you.
Have there ever been times when you felt so unusually excited, energetic, or on edge that it was clearly different from your usual self—even if it felt good or helped you get things done?

Um, well, no, I really don't think so. I mean, I try very hard to just be steady, you know? I don't think I've ever felt so... out of sorts or overly excited that I wasn't still just being me. 

I know I can get a little enthusiastic when I'm sorting inventory at work or organizing the garage, but that's just because I want to do a good job. It's not like I'm a completely different person or acting strangely. I'm just being productive. I really try to make sure I'm always acting appropriate and not making a fuss. I hope that makes sense? I just don't think I've ever been so out of character that it would be, um, clearly different from my usual self. That's a good thing, right?

Have there ever been a few days in a row where you felt unusually energized or excited, even if it felt good, where you might have been more talkative, needed less sleep, or were doing things faster or more intensely than usual?

Well, um... I guess if I'm thinking about it, there are some days where I feel... maybe a little more upbeat than usual? Like, I'll wake up feeling really good, almost like I have too much energy, and I'll think, "I can fix the whole house and reorganize the entire warehouse before dinner." And it feels wonderful, honestly, just being able to tackle everything. 

But, um... sometimes, when I'm in that kind of mood, if my husband asks a question about one of my plans or tries to slow me down, I... I might snap at him a little bit. Just over something small, you know? I always feel terrible about it right after. It's not that I'm angry, I just get so focused and moving so fast. I try really hard not to be irritable with him. Is it normal to get a little snappy when you're just trying to get a lot done? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture... I'm really not an angry person, I promise.

Can you think of a time when you felt so energized or excited that it was clearly different from your usual self—even if it felt good—where you might have been doing things faster, taking on more than usual, or felt like you didn’t need as much sleep?

Um, well... I do have days where I just have so much energy, even after work. Usually, you know, moving freight and stocking all day, a person would be completely worn out by the time they clock out. But sometimes... I don't know, I just come home buzzing. 

Instead of sitting on the couch to rest, which I probably should do, sitting just feels... impossible. Like I have to keep moving. So I'll start reorganizing the kitchen cabinets, or I'll go out to the garage and sort all the storage bins. I just get so much accomplished! It's actually really helpful to get all those chores done, you know? I hope that doesn't sound like I'm doing something wrong. It's just nice to have the energy to keep the house looking nice after a long shift. That's a good thing, isn't it?

Have there ever been times when your mood was so unusually high, you felt invincible, or you were unusually irritable along with feeling extremely energetic or active — even if it felt good — and this lasted for several days in a row?

Um, no, I don't think I've ever felt... invincible. That sounds a bit extreme, doesn't it? I mean, I know I just said I can get really focused and maybe a tiny bit irritable when I'm trying to get things done, but it's never been like I thought I had superpowers or anything like that. 

I really just try to be a hard worker and take care of my home. I don't think my mood has ever been so high that it was a problem or lasted for days and days where I was completely out of control. I'm usually pretty grounded, I think. I hope I'm not giving you the impression that I'm, you know, unstable or anything. I just try to do my best every day. Does that make sense?

Have there ever been a few days in a row where you felt unusually upbeat or irritable, had a lot more energy than usual, and found yourself doing a lot more things—like taking on extra projects or cleaning a lot—more than you normally would, even if it felt good at the time?

Well, um... I guess if you mean taking on extra things, then yes, sometimes I do that. Like at work, I've started volunteering for these extra safety-improvement projects. And outside of work, I've been signing up for a lot more art workshops than I usually would. 

I just get so motivated, you know? I'll sit down and make all these lists and schedules, almost like I'm running a whole operation or something. It feels really productive to be involved and to learn new things. I mean, it's good to be proactive at your job and have hobbies, right? I just want to make sure I'm doing things that are worthwhile. I hope that doesn't sound like I'm overdoing it... I just like to stay busy and be helpful. Is that the kind of thing you meant?

Can you recall a specific time when your mood was clearly different from usual—like feeling unusually high, elated, or irritable—while also feeling more energetic or active than normal, even if it felt good at the time?

Well, I suppose... sometimes I do get this feeling where I'm just so incredibly upbeat, almost too upbeat, if that makes sense? Like, I'll wake up and feel like I could completely fix up the whole house, and then go in and revamp everything at the warehouse, all before dinner. It's a wonderful feeling, honestly, being that capable. 

But, um... I guess there is a downside, and I feel a little bad admitting this. When I get in that zone, if my husband even just gently questions one of my big plans, I... I can snap at him. Over something completely small and silly. I always feel terrible about it afterward because he's just trying to help, and I don't want to be a difficult wife. It's just that in the moment, I'm so focused and moving so fast. I hope you don't think I'm a mean person for getting short with him like that. It's just the stress of trying to get so much done, you know? Does that sound like what you're asking about?

Can you recall a specific time when you had a distinct period—lasting several days—where your mood was clearly different from usual, like feeling unusually high, elated, or irritable, along with feeling more energetic or active than normal, even if it felt good at the time?

I mean, I know I just mentioned getting a little snappy with my husband, and having a lot of energy to do things around the house or at the warehouse, but... I don't really think I've had a time where it lasted for several days in a row and was, like, a completely different mood. 

I really try to keep things pretty steady, you know? I might have a really productive afternoon or a day where I'm just very motivated, but I don't think it's ever been a distinct period of days where I was completely unlike myself. I always try to make sure I'm doing a good job and being a good wife, and I feel like if I was acting really strange for days on end, I would notice, or my husband would say something more serious. I hope I'm answering this right... I just don't think it's ever been quite as extreme or long-lasting as what you're describing. Does that make sense?

Can you think of a time when you had a period that lasted at least four days in a row where your mood was clearly different from usual — like feeling unusually high, elated, or irritable — along with feeling much more energetic or active than normal, even if it felt good at the time?

I know you're trying to get a clear picture, and I really want to give you the right answer, but... no, I honestly can't think of a time it lasted for four days straight. Four days is almost a whole work week, you know? 

If I was acting that out of character, or... or snapping at my husband for that long, I'd feel just awful. And I'm sure someone at the warehouse would have pulled me aside if I was acting strange for that many shifts in a row. For me, it's really just a quick burst of energy to get through a busy day or organize things at home, and then I'm right back to my normal routine. 

I hope I'm not making your job harder by saying no... I just don't want to make something up if it didn't happen. Is it okay that I don't have an example like that?

Can you think of a time when you had a period that lasted at least four days in a row where your mood was clearly different from usual — like feeling unusually high, elated, or irritable — along with feeling much more energetic or active than normal, even if it felt good at the time?

Oh, gosh, I'm sorry... did I not explain that well enough just a second ago? I feel terrible if I'm not giving you what you need for your notes. 

I really have been racking my brain, but... no, I honestly still can't think of any time it went on for four whole days like that. Like I was saying, it's usually just a day or an afternoon of being really productive with the freight at work or fixing things up at home, and then it settles right back down. I'd be so embarrassed if I was acting out of sorts or snapping at my husband for almost a whole week. 

Am I... am I maybe misunderstanding what you're looking for? I really want to make sure I'm doing this right, so please let me know if I need to be thinking about this differently.
